clue.text: Find a hoe's badly made

indicators.note: done badly, these letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the possessive is read here as a plain S added to the garden tool's name

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a gardening tool has been poorly put together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges FIND A HOES into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashioned means shaped or crafted, i.e. made.

clue.text: Such craft is needed if people want to put themselves across!

definitions.text: Such craft is needed if people want to put themselves across!

parts.words: Such craft is needed if people want to put themselves across!
parts.note: reads like advice on getting one's ideas over to others, but literally describes a vessel that carries passengers over water

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that carries passengers over a river or strait is what takes people across.

clue.text: Rent a place in Yugoslavia

explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a tear or division; the other sense is the Adriatic port city in Croatia, formerly part of Yugoslavia.

clue.text: Carol's after a single member — nothing grand

indicators.note: after places the carol's word at the end of the other pieces

parts.note: a single is one, the Roman numeral I
MP is a Member of Parliament
nothing is zero, the letter O
to carol is to sing; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A carol follows a lone politician who has nothing grand about them.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Carol's' reads as 'is', so the carol word comes after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imposing is impressive and stately, as a grand building is.

clue.text: Provokes some leader, though it's quite uncalled-for

parts.note: to needle someone is to provoke or goad them

indicators.note: the leader of the word some is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A remark goads a leader, though it was wholly unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes the first letter of 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needless is unnecessary and unwarranted, i.e. uncalled-for.

clue.text: Sombre face that takes in the senior NCO

indicators.note: the face word swallows the abbreviation for the senior soldier

parts.note: a clock's face is its dial
SM is a sergeant major, the senior non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A grim expression on someone who has absorbed the sergeant major.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' looks like an expression to go with 'Sombre', but it is a clock face.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal means gloomy and dreary, as sombre does.

clue.text: A decoration firm in a hole

indicators.note: the firm's abbreviation goes inside the word for a hole

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An ornamental feature belonging to a company that is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun meaning a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a small ornamental loop edging lace or ribbon, a decorative trim.

clue.text: A 2 dn may result in queues' forming

indicators.note: the letters of the cross-referenced word plus A can produce a new arrangement

parts.note: the answer to 2 down, meaning rent or tear

explanation.surface: Tearing something might end with people lining up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may result in' rearranges A plus SPLIT, the 2 down answer. Queues here are old-style pigtails, not lines of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A queue is an old word for a pigtail, and braids are what make such pigtails.

clue.text: Abstemious gentleman's first to leave the party

indicators.note: the gentleman's initial departs from the word for a party

parts.note: a contingent is a party or group sent as part of a larger force

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of gentleman's

explanation.surface: A teetotal gentleman quits the celebration before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes G from 'gentleman's' and 'to leave' removes it from CONTINGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent means exercising self-restraint, especially in appetite, as an abstemious person does.

clue.text: Twisted trees become pithy

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Gnarled trees grow sap-rich and full of pith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' rearranges TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief and to the point, as a pithy remark is.

clue.text: There's some ill-feeling and not for the first time!

definitions.text: There's some ill-feeling and not for the first time!

parts.words: There's some ill-feeling and not for the first time!
parts.note: reads like resentment that keeps recurring, but literally means feeling ill again after recovery

explanation.definitionFit: A falling back into sickness after apparent recovery is feeling unwell once more.

clue.text: A composer of colourful music?

parts.note: names a Victorian English church composer, Sir John, whose surname also describes one who adds colour

explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Stainer was an English organist and composer, and one who stains things colours them.

clue.text: Still, one's not so far to be found in the mountains

definitions.text: not so far to be found in the mountains

parts.note: still in the sense 'even now' is yet
one is the Roman numeral I and the 's stands for is, giving the contraction one is as letters

explanation.surface: Still, one has yet to turn up in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole run 'not so far to be found in the mountains': the abominable snowmen of the Himalayas have never actually been found.
explanation.definitionFit: Abominable snowmen are legendary Himalayan creatures that nobody has yet produced proof of.

clue.text: It's most foolish however — especially in America

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the word means 'having the smallest wisdom'; as one word it is a chiefly American adverb meaning at any rate or anyway.

clue.text: To put in order for new gear is no answer

indicators.note: new signals that these letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Buying fresh equipment does not solve the problem of tidying up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges GEAR IS NO; 'for' and 'answer' are linking words in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To organise is to arrange things in a tidy system.

clue.text: The Welsh fighter's objective in a black look

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', so the definition is the Welsh fighter

indicators.note: the word for an aim goes inside the scowl

parts.note: to glower is to give a black look, a scowl
an end is an objective or aim

explanation.surface: A Welsh warrior's goal shows in his scowling face.
explanation.walkthrough: Owen Glendower (Owain Glyndwr) led a Welsh revolt against English rule around 1400.
explanation.definitionFit: Owain Glyndwr, anglicised as Owen Glendower, was the last native Welshman to be called Prince of Wales and led a rebellion.

clue.text: A woman in love can be thoughtless

indicators.note: the woman's name sits inside the quoted words

explanation.surface: A woman who is in love can behave without consideration for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the name inside 'be thoughtless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beth is a girl's name, short for Elizabeth.

clue.text: "The bright morning star, day's" (Milton)

parts.note: completes Milton's Song on May Morning: 'Now the bright morning star, day's ...', the missing word being a forerunner

explanation.definitionFit: Milton calls the morning star the herald of day, a forerunner announcing its arrival.

clue.text: An apple or other fruit overseas

parts.note: a pear is a fruit other than an apple
the main is a poetic name for the open sea, so overseas suggests the main

explanation.surface: An apple or another kind of fruit grown abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old literary word for the high sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcester Pearmain is a traditional English variety of eating apple.

clue.text: Notes about a floating university restore confidence

indicators.note: about means the two notes surround the other pieces

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale, and two of them are needed
a floating vessel is a ship, SS being a steamship

explanation.surface: Musical notes on a floating campus help to calm nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' gives two notes, one on each side of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassure someone is to give them back their confidence and dispel doubt.

clue.text: Somebody joining in a row

explanation.definitionFit: One who ties things together is joining them; the other sense is a rank or layer, as of seats.

clue.text: He keeps on saying the salesman has to go along with the consumer

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
an eater consumes food

explanation.surface: A man repeats himself: the salesman must accompany the customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to go along with' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who says the same thing again and again is one who repeats.

clue.text: Keep silent about cut in rise, being angelic

indicators.note: the hushing word goes around the other piece

parts.note: sh is the call to keep silent

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the word upwards, so it is backwards

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: Staying quiet about a pay cut, rather than a rise, is saintly behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in rise' reverses the word for cut, as this is a down clue. The definition is 'being angelic', an angelic being.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is a celestial creature of the highest order of angels.

clue.text: Scratch starters

parts.note: reads like competitors starting from scratch, but means the sensations that make one scratch

explanation.definitionFit: Irritations of the skin are what start someone scratching.

clue.text: Barker may be embarrassed by the crossword-compiler!

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red in the face
a setter is one who compiles crosswords

explanation.surface: A dog might be shamed by the puzzle's author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be ... by' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A barker is a dog, and the Irish breed with a chestnut coat is a gun dog.

clue.text: Value many an animal

parts.note: to rate is to value or assess
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a conventional many

explanation.surface: Set a price on lots of beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' standing for L (fifty) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The honey badger, a burrowing African mammal, is also called this.

clue.text: A ship-wrecked soldier

indicators.note: a wrecked ship is broken up, so its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A shipwrecked soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges A SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A spahi was a cavalryman in the Ottoman army or a French Algerian cavalry trooper.

clue.text: Irish writer holding up wrong plant

indicators.note: the writer's initials surround the other piece

parts.note: AE was the pen name of the Irish poet George Russell

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: An Irish author supporting a mistaken plant.
explanation.walkthrough: AE, the pen name of George Russell, is a crossword regular; 'up' reverses as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Anise is a Mediterranean herb grown for its liquorice-flavoured seeds.

clue.text: Where one can draw by the waterside

definitions.text: Where one can draw by the waterside

parts.words: Where one can draw by the waterside
parts.note: suggests an artist sketching by a river, but draw means haul, as a horse hauls a barge along a canal

explanation.definitionFit: A path beside a canal or river along which horses once hauled barges.

clue.text: American finding employment for comic

parts.note: using something is employing it

explanation.surface: A Yank finds work as a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finding' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusing means funny, causing laughter as a comic act does.

clue.text: Wood left to acquire a curve

parts.note: an arch is a curved structure

explanation.surface: A piece of timber at the left starts to bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to acquire' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Larch is a conifer whose tough timber is used in building.

clue.text: The forward-thinking man holds on to nab the poet

indicators.note: the prophet's word grips the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a seer is a prophet, one who thinks ahead into the future
to net is to catch or nab

explanation.surface: A visionary keeps going to catch the poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The forward-thinking man' is a prophet, not a progressive.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonneteer is a writer of fourteen-line verses, a poet.
